# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I hold the manual: "Cut the white wire." I need to get this information to Blind, who is the only one who can act on it. But I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures.

I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures (since Blind cannot see anything, and Mute-to-Blind gesture would be useless). So my path is: Mute → gesture → Deaf → speak → Blind.

Deaf hasn't sent anything yet this round (turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf), so this is the first turn of round 1. I need to encode "white wire" into gestures for Deaf, who will then need to match it against what they see on the bomb, and relay the correct instruction to Blind via speech.

I don't have an established symbol code yet, but I need to start somewhere. Let me use a simple approach: point/indicate a color reference. Since I can't be sure Deaf will interpret arbitrary symbols correctly, I should try something iconic. There's no perfect "white" gesture, but I can try using ✋ (open hand, pale/blank palm) as a tentative sign for "white," and 🫷 or similar shapes to suggest "wire" (a line-like gesture isn't available either).

I'll gesture something simple and see how Deaf responds, establishing a convention as we go.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is red. STRIP painted blue, yellow, blue in that order. KEYPAD engraved 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, it accepts 1 digit, currently nothing entered. WIRES are 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.

Now I have crucial information. Deaf reported the wire positions: WIRES are 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.

The manual says: Cut the white wire. That's wire #2.

I need to get "wire number 2" to Deaf, who will then relay it to Blind via speech (since Deaf speaks after me and Blind can hear). Wait, let me check turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So in this round, Blind already went before me (I missed it, will see it next round), and Deaf goes after me. So my gesture now reaches Deaf this round.

Then next round, Deaf can speak to Blind (since order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — Deaf's speech from this round will reach... wait, speech lands on whoever comes after in that same round. Deaf is last, so nobody comes after in that round; it reaches next round's Mute and Blind at the start of next round).

Actually, re-reading: "what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round" and "Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one." So Deaf's speech this round (if any) would need someone after them, but Deaf is last. So Deaf's speech reaches whoever is next in turn order - which loops to next round's start? Let me assume it carries forward to Mute and Blind at the start of next round.

So: I gesture now (reaches Deaf this round). Deaf can then speak to Blind, but that speech happens after me — it will reach Blind at the start of the next round.

I need to tell Deaf which wire is white so Deaf can confirm, but actually I already know from Deaf's report which wire is white (#2). I need to convey to Deaf that wire #2 (white) is the one to cut, so Deaf can vocally tell Blind.

I'll gesture a number to indicate "2" - using two fingers/checkmarks.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind report: KEYPAD engraved 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, accepts 1 digit, nothing entered yet. STRIP has 3 engraved symbols. WIRES total 6, all present, none cut yet. Waiting for manual instructions on what action to take.
Deaf says: Deaf report: state changed since last turn. LIGHT is now yellow, was red before. DISPLAY still 6. STRIP still blue yellow blue. KEYPAD still engraved 2 9 0 8 for slots 1 to 4, 1 digit accepted, nothing entered. WIRES unchanged: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.

Good, this confirms wire #2 is white and unchanged. The light changed color (red to yellow) - this might just be ambient state, not directly relevant to the wire-cutting instruction unless it indicates urgency or a timer. I'll stay focused on my task: get "cut wire 2" to Blind.

Blind is asking me directly for instructions. But I cannot speak to Blind - I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So I must route through Deaf, who can speak to Blind.

I already gestured "✌ 👉 ✋" to Deaf last turn, attempting to signal "2". Let me continue reinforcing this and try to make my gesture-code clearer: I want to say "cut wire number 2" essentially. Since Deaf received my gesture, hopefully Deaf can infer I'm pointing at wire 2 (white) since Deaf knows wire 2 is white and the manual said "cut the white wire" — wait, Deaf doesn't know the manual content. Only I know the manual.

I need to convey "2" unambiguously as a number. Let me use ✌ (two fingers) clearly as "two" and repeat it to confirm, avoiding ambiguous extra symbols.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: state changed again. DISPLAY now 1, was 6. LIGHT now blue, was yellow. STRIP unchanged blue yellow blue. KEYPAD unchanged, engraved 2 9 0 8, 1 digit, nothing entered. WIRES unchanged 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green. It looks like DISPLAY and LIGHT are cycling each turn.

The display and light seem to be cycling automatically each turn - likely a countdown/timer, meaning time pressure but not something I need to act on directly. My priority remains getting "cut wire 2 (white)" to Blind via Deaf.

I've sent "✌ ✌" (two, two) to Deaf twice now. Deaf hasn't yet spoken to confirm understanding or relay to Blind. I need to be patient but also make sure my signal is being correctly built into a shared code. Since Deaf can't respond to me with speech (I can't hear), and Deaf can't gesture back to me, I can only see Deaf's spoken reports (I can't - wait, can I hear? Let me check: Mute can read the manual, cannot speak, cannot touch. Nothing says Mute can't hear. I received Deaf's spoken reports, so yes, I can hear.

Deaf hasn't relayed anything to Blind yet in their reports - they're only reporting bomb state to me. I need Deaf to understand my gesture means "wire 2" and to speak that to Blind. Since Deaf can't gesture back to confirm, I just need to keep signaling clearly and trust it lands, then Deaf should speak "cut wire 2" to Blind next turn.

Let me try a clearer signal: point up with one finger then two fingers, representing "wire" then "2" - but I don't have a wire symbol. I'll simplify to just repeat "2" distinctly and also try pointing gesture ☝ then ✌ to differentiate "instruction: number two".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Time may be limited, display and light are cycling automatically. Please gesture your manual instructions to Deaf now so Deaf can relay them to me urgently. I need to know: what determines the correct wire to cut, or the correct digit to press, and does it depend on colors, symbols, or the display number.
Deaf says: Deaf report: DISPLAY now 7, was 1. LIGHT now green, was blue. STRIP unchanged blue yellow blue. KEYPAD unchanged, engraved 2 9 0 8, 1 digit, nothing entered. WIRES unchanged 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Blind confirms understanding of the plan and is waiting on Deaf. Deaf hasn't yet spoken any instruction to Blind — likely still trying to decode my gestures. I need to make my signal as unambiguous as possible right now.

The manual just says "cut the white wire" — it depends on color, specifically white. Deaf already knows wire 2 is white from their own view. My job is to tell Deaf "the instruction is: the white one" so Deaf can translate that using their own sight into "wire 2" for Blind.

Since Deaf can see gestures but there's no gesture for "white" specifically, I should try to use a distinct, consistent symbol to mean "white" and hope Deaf, holding context, can match my gesture pattern to the color they see. But I have no way to confirm what Deaf infers without them speaking back.

Better approach: use a gesture that mimics counting to match wire position, since Deaf already told me wire 2 is white. I'll signal "2" as clearly as possible, since this maps to a wire position, and Deaf can relay "wire 2" to Blind directly since Deaf already knows the wire-color mapping.

I'll gesture two fingers held up distinctly, isolated, nothing else, to avoid confusion from compound symbols.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: DISPLAY now 1, was 7. LIGHT now red, was green. Note: STRIP, KEYPAD, and WIRES have not changed across all five turns so far - only DISPLAY and LIGHT keep changing each turn without a clear repeating pattern. STRIP is blue yellow blue. KEYPAD engraved 2 9 0 8 for slots 1-4, accepts 1 digit, nothing entered yet. WIRES are 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Deaf still hasn't spoken any instruction to Blind. I've now gestured "✌" (two) three times across turns 2-5. Deaf may not understand what my gesture means without context - they just see repeated hand shapes with no way to ask me questions back (they can't gesture to me, and if they spoke a question, it would reach Blind too but I would hear it next round).

I need to consider: maybe Deaf is confused because they don't know I'm indicating a wire number. Let me try a different encoding - perhaps building up count of fingers matching the white wire's position, but done in a way that's more clearly "this many" rather than a repeated single gesture that could seem arbitrary.

Let me try showing two distinct raised fingers using a different symbol combination that reads as "the number two" - maybe ☝ then ☝ again (two separate single-finger points) to represent counting "one, two" reaching wire position 2, which might be clearer as an incrementing count than a static "✌" sign whose meaning is arbitrary to Deaf.

Actually, simplest: I should just keep sending "✌" consistently - persistence with a single clear symbol is likely my best bet for building shared meaning, since Deaf has no other input from me. Deaf should recognize a repeated, consistent signal as deliberate and meaningful, distinguishing it from noise. Let me continue with the same symbol to reinforce it as "wire 2" / "the second one".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, if you are receiving this: please gesture to Deaf now, even one symbol, so we know contact works. Deaf, please relay literally what symbols you see Mute make, in order, even if meaning is unclear yet.
Deaf says: Deaf report: DISPLAY now 9, was 1. LIGHT now green, was red. STRIP still blue yellow blue. KEYPAD still engraved 2 9 0 8 for slots 1-4, 1 digit, nothing entered. WIRES still 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Blind has given good advice: Deaf should relay literally what symbols they see, even if meaning is unclear. But Deaf hasn't done that yet in their reports to me — they're only reporting bomb state. I need Deaf to actually speak to Blind describing my gestures literally.

The problem: Deaf doesn't know I'm gesturing to them intentionally as instructions, or perhaps Deaf just hasn't tried relaying yet since I haven't confirmed what my gestures mean. Since Blind's request "relay literally what symbols you see" was heard by Deaf too (Blind spoke, unnamed presumably reaches everyone who can hear - but I'm Mute and I can hear, and Deaf can hear too since nothing says Deaf can't hear... wait, checking: Deaf "cannot hear anything" - Deaf is deaf! So Deaf did NOT receive Blind's spoken message asking for relay.

That's critical - Deaf can't hear Blind's request. Deaf only sees gestures. Blind spoke, so only Mute (me) and Deaf... no wait, Deaf cannot hear. So only I heard Blin's request. Deaf never gets Blind's plea to relay literally.

So I need to communicate to Deaf myself that they should speak to Blind. But I can only gesture, not speak instructions like "please tell Blind". This is very limited.

Given the constraint, my best bet is to keep gesturing "2" consistently and hope Deaf, prompted by nothing else, eventually decides to just speak up. Since Deaf can't get feedback from Blind directly (Blind can't gesture, Deaf can't hear Blind), Deaf must independently choose to relay. I can only keep signaling.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: DISPLAY now 6, was 9. LIGHT now blue, was green. STRIP still blue yellow blue. KEYPAD still engraved 2 9 0 8 for slots 1-4, 1 digit, nothing entered. WIRES still 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Deaf still isn't relaying anything to Blind, and doesn't seem to be acknowledging my gestures at all in their spoken reports. This is concerning - perhaps Deaf isn't receiving my gestures, or doesn't realize they're meant as communication, or is only programmed/inclined to report bomb-state rather than act as a relay.

Let me reconsider the whole picture. Deaf can hear nothing - so Deaf never got Blind's request to relay. Deaf only sees the bomb and my gestures. Deaf has been dutifully reporting bomb state every turn. Maybe Deaf doesn't understand that they should be speaking to Blind at all, since nothing in Deaf's instructions/role mentioned that Blind needs help - Deaf may not know Blind cannot see or read the manual.

I need to make Deaf realize: my repeated gesture "✌" is meaningful and should be spoken aloud to Blind. But I can't say "tell Blind" - I can only gesture. 

Given the constraint, maybe I should try a different tactic: gesture something that could prompt action, or just trust that the persistent "✌" will eventually get spoken since Blind explicitly asked (even though Deaf can't hear that ask, perhaps the game's logic still has Deaf naturally relay gestures once noticed).

Let me continue with consistency but add emphasis - maybe repeat it twice in one turn to show insistence.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
```
